findings.title: Checkpoints 3.2a and 3.7 cannot pass: tests of the removed behaviour are deleted too late
findings.description:
Tasks 3.1–3.2 stop rendering the `Comprehension:` line and the Adoption Facts section. Task 3.2a (task file lines 99–101) then requires `pnpm --filter @context-forge/core test` to pass and commits. Two existing test files still assert that output at that point:

- **`pipeline-integration.test.ts:124-190`**: the "brownfield build with an injected squadron probe" block expects the probe JSON, the `- Squadron: unavailable…` statement and `Comprehension: …` in the output. The plan deletes this block in 3.3, after the 3.2a checkpoint.
- **`adoptionBuild.integration.test.ts`**: `expectBrownfield` (line 99) requires `### Adoption Facts`, and cases 3, 4, 5b, 6, 8, 9b, 9c, 11 and 13 use it. The plan deletes this file in 4.1.

The same file breaks 3.7 (lines 131–134), which requires `pnpm -r test` to pass before the seam-removal commit:

- After 3.3 the hook is gone, so every brownfield case returns the concept prompt.
- Case 12 (`rejects.toBeInstanceOf(AdoptionError)`) no longer rejects.
- Tests are not typechecked, so the extra `options` argument at line 68 is silently ignored and the file still runs.

As written, a junior either stops at 3.2a or deletes tests ad hoc, and both commits land on a red suite.

Fix: move the deletion of `adoptionBuild.integration.test.ts` and the `pipeline-integration.test.ts` brownfield block into 3.1/3.2. Alternatively, drop the 3.2a commit, fold 3.1–3.2 into the 3.7 commit, and delete `adoptionBuild.integration.test.ts` in 3.3. The other three test files in 4.1 call `createAdoptionResolver` and the facts/completion functions directly and can stay there.

findings.title: The 6.2 export audit would remove `measureSourceVolume`, which the plan and design keep
findings.description:
Task 6.2 (line 200) says to remove any export from `adoption/index.ts` or `detection/index.ts` with no production consumer, unless it belongs to `history`, `comprehensionAnalysis` or `adoptionOutcome`.

- `measureSourceVolume` has exactly one production caller today: `adoptionResolver.ts:12,61`, which 4.1 deletes.
- The design's stated consumer for `sourceVolume` (slice line 68, `discoverDocs`) imports only `EXCLUDED_DIRS` from that file (`docs-map/discoverDocs.ts:9`), and `EXCLUDED_DIRS` is not in the index.
- So the audit, applied literally, tells the junior to drop `measureSourceVolume` and `SourceVolume` from the public index.
- That contradicts task 4.1, which rewrites `outOfTreeLinks.test.ts` against `measureSourceVolume`, and the design's Patterns section (slice line 145), which lists it as kept.

Fix: name `measureSourceVolume`/`SourceVolume` as retained in 6.2 and the Context Summary. Also say whether the audit is per symbol or per module; `adoption/index.ts` is `export *`, so there is no export list to trim there.

findings.title: Test files are outside typecheck and lint, so leftover references in tests are unverified
findings.description:
`tsc --noEmit` includes only `src/**/*` in every package, and `eslint.config.mjs:9` ignores `**/tests/**`. Vitest strips types, so a call such as `createContextPipeline(path, { adoptionStateWrites: 'read-only' })` keeps running after the signature change.

- 3.4 (lines 114–115) tells the junior to remove remaining test references, but its success check is the core typecheck, which cannot see tests.
- The 6.2 grep (line 198) covers `packages/*/src` only.

Concrete survivors if a step is missed:

- `ContextTemplateEngine.test.ts:236-245`: the "adds nothing" cases pass `adoptionFacts`. They do not match 3.2's "renders or is placed" wording and pass trivially.
- `CoreServiceFactory.test.ts`: six call sites pass the options argument.
- `cli/tests/integration/build.integration.test.ts:42-65`: four call sites pass it.

Fix: run the 6.2 grep over `packages/*/tests` as well (same `COMPREHENSION_PROFILE_VARIABLE` exception plus the `brownfield-guide` fixture profile line). In 3.2, say the whole `adoption facts (slice 261)` describe block goes.

findings.title: The 6.3 walkthrough leaves a registered project in the real store and does not say how to build the scratch repo
findings.description:
Walkthrough step 1 needs a repo "registered with `cf init`" in Phase 0, with the guide installed and more than 2000 source lines. Task 6.3 (lines 204–205) only says "in a scratch brownfield repo under `/tmp`" and resets `adoption.state`.

- Running `cf init` with the default data dir writes a project entry for `/tmp/bf-scratch` into the developer's real `projects.json`.
- No step removes that entry or the scratch directory.
- A junior is also not told how to produce the repo (guide install, phase, source file).

Fix: have 6.3 export `CONTEXT_FORGE_DATA_DIR` to a temp directory for the walkthrough (the store honours it), list the setup commands, and delete both temp directories at the end.

findings.title: Commit markers are written as checkboxes
findings.description:
Every commit point is a checkbox: task 2.3 (line 79), and the `- [ ] Commit:` items at lines 101, 134, 148, 155, 163, 169, 186 and 206. The convention is a plain `**Commit**:` line, never a checkbox. Task 3.2a exists only to hold a commit and a success line.

Fix: convert these to plain `**Commit**:` lines after the relevant task, and drop 2.3 and 3.2a as tasks.

findings.title: Three statements about existing tests and callers are inaccurate
findings.description:
- **3.3 (line 106)** says to delete "the options and adoption-wiring cases" in `CoreServiceFactory.test.ts`. There are none; the file only passes `{ adoptionStateWrites: 'read-only' }` at six call sites (lines 29, 35, 59, 99, 119, 141), which need updating.
- **3.6 (line 128)** says to delete "the adoption and probe cases" in `contextTools.test.ts`. There are two adoption cases (lines 176 and 371) and no probe cases.
- **3.6 (line 125)** says to update the `registerContextTools` caller "in the server setup". `mcp-server/src/index.ts:40` already calls `registerContextTools(server)` with no options; the only caller passing options is `tests/helpers/integrationSetup.ts:41`.

findings.title: Smaller gaps in 2.2, 4.3 and 5.1
findings.description:
- **4.3**: "delete the write cases and keep the read cases" removes `round-trips %j`, the only direct test that `readAdoptionState` returns each valid stored value. Indirect coverage remains through the navigation fixtures. Consider re-seeding that case with a hand-written TOML file instead.
- **5.1**: the test must seed `adoption.state = "in_progress"`, but `writeAdoptionState` is deleted in 4.3. Say to write the TOML directly or use `ConfigManager.set`.
- **5.1**: `pureBuild.test.ts` resolves `@context-forge/core/node` from `dist/`, last built at 3.7. Add `pnpm --filter @context-forge/core build` before the run so it exercises the post-section-4 core. 6.1 does rebuild, so the final result is still valid.
- **2.2 Case 2**: titled "planned at Phase 4" but sets only instruction `design`. State whether `developmentPhase` should be `Phase 4: Slice Design`.

findings.title: Root `pnpm typecheck` in 4.1–4.4 checks cli and mcp against a stale core build
findings.description: `cli` and `mcp-server` resolve core through `dist/`, as the task file states at line 87. Section 4 never rebuilds core, so the root typecheck there proves nothing about those two packages. There is no actual break: after 3.6 neither package's `src` imports a symbol that section 4 removes, and 6.1 rebuilds first.
